They wear worldly garments while delighting in fine monastic robes;
they don clothes of five colors,
drink wine, roast meat, and kill living beings out of greed for flavor.
Lacking any heart of compassion, they harbored mutual hatred and envy.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva who cultivated virtue through diligent effort;
all revered him and looked to him as their guide.
He taught with impartiality, taking pity on the poor and being mindful of the elderly;
he rescued and nurtured those in distress and poverty, constantly providing them with scriptures and images,
and leading people to serve these objects of veneration and cultivate all manner of merit.
His disposition was gentle and virtuous, never harming others;
he sacrificed his own body to save sentient beings without cherishing himself,
practicing patience, benevolence, and harmony.
Should there be such a person, the hosts of Māras and bhikṣus will all together harbor jealousy toward them.
They will slander and propagate evil reports about them, ostracizing and expelling them so that they may not remain.
Thereafter, they themselves will no longer cultivate the Way or its virtues.
The temples lie deserted and ruined, no longer repaired and falling further into decay;
yet they greedily hoard wealth and goods without dispersing it,
failing to cultivate merit while instead trafficking in slaves.
They plow fields and plant crops, burning down mountains and forests;
they harm sentient beings without a heart of compassion.
Servants become bhikṣus, and maidservants become bhikṣuṇīs.
There is no morality or virtue;
lustful excess and turbid disorder prevail, with no distinction made between men and women.
That the Way has become thin and insipid is entirely due to such people.
Some, seeking to evade the local authorities,
rely upon our Way to become bhikṣus without cultivating the precepts;
at the end of each half-month, they merely go through the motions of reciting the code of discipline.
They become weary and indolent, having no desire to listen;
they abridge the beginning and end of the sutras, refusing to explain them in their entirety, and do not recite them.
Even if there are those who do read them, they do not understand the words and phrases, yet they insist on speaking as if they did.
Without consulting those of wisdom, they are arrogant and seek fame;
they puff themselves up with haughty strides, regarding this as honor and nobility while hoping for the offerings of others.
After these demonic bhikṣus pass away, [they will fall into the hells].
Their spirits shall fall into the Avīci Hell for the five heinous crimes;
they will pass through every realm of hungry ghosts and animals throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Only after their offenses have ended do they emerge,
being born in a borderland where the Three Jewels do not exist.
At a time when the Dharma is about to perish, women will apply themselves with diligence and constantly perform meritorious deeds.
The men were indolent and arrogant, refusing to heed the words of the Dharma;
they looked upon śramaṇas as if seeing dung and soil,
lacking any faith, so that the Wheel of the Dharma was submerged.
At that time, the devas wept tears;
the rains and droughts were irregular, the five grains did not ripen,
pestilence spread, and those who died were numerous.
The people toil in hardship while local officials oppress and exploit them;
they do not cultivate the Way and all long for chaos.
Evil people increase by the day, while those who are good are exceedingly few.
The sun and moon turn ever more swiftly, and human life grows ever shorter.
By the age of forty, one’s hair is white, yet one barely reaches sixty years of age.
Men have short lifespans, while women have long lives.
They live for seventy, eighty, ninety, or even a hundred years;
yet a great flood may suddenly arise without warning, arriving at an unforeseen time.
Because people of the world do not believe this, they claim that things are permanent.
The various classes of sentient beings, without distinction between noble and base,
were submerged, drifting, and devoured by fish and turtles;
the Bodhisattva and the assembly of bhikṣus were driven away by Māra.
Without participating in the assemblies, the Bodhisattva entered the mountains;
dwelling in a place of merit, maintaining himself in tranquility,
he found joy therein and his lifespan was extended.
The various devas protected Candra-prabha’s appearance in the world;
they encountered one another and together promoted my Way for fifty-two years.
The Śūraṅgama Sūtra and the Pratyutpanna Samādhi first vanished through transformation;
the twelve divisions of the scriptures soon followed and likewise vanished.
All things will no longer appear and written characters will not be seen.
The saffron robes of the śramaṇas will naturally turn white.
After the departure of the Holy King, my Dharma will be completely extinguished.
It is like an oil lamp which, when it is about to go out,
its light becomes even more intense before it finally extinguishes;
the exhaustion of my Dharma will be just like the extinction of that lamp.
From this point onward, it would be difficult to record [the events] in detail.
After such a long time,
Maitreya will descend into the world and become a Buddha.
The world was at peace, poisonous vapors were eliminated, and rains fell with harmonious moderation, causing the five grains to flourish.
Trees grew tall, and humans reached a height of eight zhang;
all lived for eighty-four thousand years.
Sentient beings who have attained deliverance are beyond measure.
You have certainly established through the Vaipulya sutras that the Three Jewels are eternally abiding.
According to the principle of the eternally abiding Dharma, there is no arising or ceasing.
The coming of rise and extinction is merely the result of worldly conditions and karma.
Departing from the West in the morning does not harm the constant radiance of the thousand lights.
*Śākyamuni-purva* (The Genealogy of Śākyamuni), Scroll Five.
